about: The commemoration of the living. In old Rome the names of those for whom the offering was made were read from tablets called diptychs; the missal's N. et N. is what remains of them. The priest joins his hands and falls silent — he prays for those he means to remember, and no one hears the names. The prayer then takes in all who are present, circumstántes, literally those standing round, and sets out what is asked for them: the redeeming of their souls, their hope of salvation, and their safety.

s01.translation: Be mindful, O Lord, of thy servants and handmaids

s02.narrative: The priest joins his hands and prays a while in silence for those he means to remember; then he spreads his hands and goes on.

s03.translation: and of all here present, whose faith is known to thee and whose devotion is not hidden, for whom we offer to thee:

s04.translation: or who themselves offer thee this sacrifice of praise, for themselves and for all their own: for the redemption of their souls, for their hope of salvation and safety,

s05.translation: and who pay their vows to thee, the eternal, living and true God.

w001.function: A future imperative — the only one this verb has; Latin uses it to mean “have this in mind when the moment comes”.

w003.function: A genitive, because meminísse governs the genitive: to be mindful of someone.

w004.function: One written word: the feminine noun with -que (and) attached. Liturgical Latin names the men and the women separately.

w005.function: Here the missal prints N. et N.; the priest passes into silence and calls the names to mind, and no one hears them.

w008.function: A participle used as a noun: literally those standing round. That is what Church Latin calls the congregation.

w013.function: One est serves both clauses: the faith is known and the devotion is not hidden.

w021.function: Vel allows both alternatives; aut would rule one of them out. The offering is made by the priest for them and by them through him.

w027.function: Sacrifícium laudis is a phrase from the psalms (Ps 49 and 115) taken into the Canon.

w029.function: The reflexive marks neither number nor gender: one form serves for one and for many, and only its case is fixed, by the preposition.

w030.function: The masculine comes from the sense — people, not things; the form itself marks no gender.

w033.function: From émere, to buy; a redémptio is the buying back of a slave for a price.

w038.function: Salus means salvation and health at once; beside it stands incolúmitas, safety in this life — the prayer asks for both.

w043.function: Vota réddere is a technical phrase: to discharge a vow made to a god, to pay what was promised.

w047.function: Dative: it is to him that the vows are paid. The pair living and true comes from the Old Testament and sets God against the idols.
